useWhen: Use WEAPON when the source is something a creature attacks with and it has weapon damage: a mundane or magic sword, bow or other weapon, a monster's natural weapon (bite, claw), an improvised weapon or a siege weapon. A magic staff that can be swung as a quarterstaff is a weapon even when it is mainly a spellcasting focus: write `ITEM.Base Weapon: quarterstaff`, and `PROPERTIES.Focus: true` if the source says it can be a focus.
smallest: `ITEM.Name` (the name), `ITEM.Weapon Type` (one of `simpleM`, `simpleR`, `martialM`, `martialR`, `natural`, `improv`, `siege`), `ITEM.Base Weapon` (required for the first four types; leave it out for `natural`, `improv` and `siege`), `DAMAGE.DAMAGE_DATA` (all ten keys; `Dice Count`, `Die Denomination` and `Damage Types` hold the weapon die).
notFor: Arrows, bolts, sling bullets and other ammunition: CONSUMABLE (`Consumable Type: ammo`).
A wand or rod. It has no weapon damage: EQUIPMENT (`Equipment Type: wand` or `rod`).
A worn item that only improves attacks (bracers, gloves, a ring): EQUIPMENT.
A spell that makes an attack: SPELL.
A monster ability with no weapon attack (breath weapon, aura, Multiattack): FEAT.
Poison or oil that is applied to a weapon: CONSUMABLE.

checks: Write `ITEM.Weapon Type` with exact case: `simpleM`, `simpleR`, `martialM`, `martialR`. `martialm` or `Martial Melee` fails.

Write `ITEM.Base Weapon` as the mundane weapon in one lowercase word: `longsword`, `lightcrossbow`, `handcrossbow`, `warpick`. Use it for magic weapons too. Spaces are removed (`hand crossbow` becomes `handcrossbow`), and an id dnd5e does not know gives a warning.

Write all ten `DAMAGE_DATA` keys. For a plain weapon the other seven are `Bonus: ""`, `Modifiers: []`, `Custom Enabled: false`, `Custom Formula: ""`, `Scaling Mode: none`, `Scaling Dice Count: 0`, `Scaling Formula: ""`.

Put only the weapon's own die in `DAMAGE.DAMAGE_DATA`. Leave `Bonus` empty: do not write the ability modifier or the magic bonus there. Extra damage that depends on a condition (for example 2d6 fire while the blade burns) does not belong in `DAMAGE_DATA`.

`PROPERTIES.Versatile: true` needs `VERSATILE_DAMAGE.DAMAGE_DATA`, and `PROPERTIES.Ammunition: true` needs `AMMUNITION.Ammunition Type`. The import fails without them. Ammunition ids are case-sensitive: `arrow`, `crossbowBolt`, `firearmBullet`, `slingBullet`, `energyCell`, `blowgunNeedle`.
`PROPERTIES.Reach` is `true` or `false`; the distance is the number in `RANGE.Reach`. `RANGE.Range Normal` and `RANGE.Range Long` are separate numbers: write `20` and `60`, never `20/60`.

Write damage types in lowercase (`slashing`, not `Slashing`) and property keys exactly as in the reference (`Two-Handed` has a hyphen). A wrong damage type fails. A wrong property key is ignored with a warning.

Set `PROPERTIES.Magical: true` on every magic weapon; `ATTUNEMENT.Attunement: required` does not set it. `ATTUNEMENT.Magic Bonus` is a number such as `1`, never dice. Always write `ITEM.Rarities` (`[]` for a mundane weapon; a missing key is stored as `common`) and `INVENTORY.Identified` (a missing key follows the user's setting).
